newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania to pay compensation over ferry tragedy.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania to pay compensation over ferry tragedy.

text.p: Tanzania's government will start paying compensation next month to survivors and families of victims of a shipping disaster on Lake Victoria in which over 600 people died, a newspaper said on Saturday.
The independent Guardian daily quoted Mwanza Regional Commissioner Major-General James Luhanga as saying 32.4 million Tanzanian shillings had been allocated so far as compensation.

Luhanga said the family of each of the dead would receive 500,000 shillings ($833) and survivors a minimum of 100,000 shillings ($166). Payments would start on March 3 with compensation for 153 victims and 59 survivors.
More than 600 people died in May last year when the ferry Bukoba capsized and sank in 27 metres (90 feet) of water in Africa's largest lake. A total of 403 bodies were recovered.

A government inquiry blamed the ship's owners, the state -owned Tanzania Railways Corporation, for operating an unstable ship and said its marine operations were characterised by gross negligence, inefficiency, corruption and other malpractices.

Disasters involving overloaded boats are common on the lake, covering 70,000-square-km (27,000-square-miles) from Uganda in the north to Tanzania in the south and Kenya in the east. ($1=600 Tanzanian shillings)
